parameters.name: Installed capacity
parameters.description: Nameplate DC capacity of PV plant
parameters.source: Averta Excel model — Ejemplo 100 kW v2.86
parameters.notes: Standardized ~100 kW nominal. Actual sizing per rooftop.

parameters.name: Specific yield (P50)
parameters.description: Annual energy production per kWp installed — P50 estimate
parameters.source: Portfolio-weighted PVGIS P50, recalibrated 2026-03-01 from pvgis_stochastic.yaml multi-tilt
parameters.notes: Recalibrated from zone-specific PVGIS data with optimal tilts. Sigma = 8% interannual (zone-weighted portfolio variance). P90 yield ≈ mu - 1.28*sigma ≈ 1417 kWh/kWp.

parameters.name: Annual degradation rate
parameters.description: Year-over-year production decline from panel aging
parameters.source: Averta Excel model (0.35%/yr). Industry range 0.3-0.7% for mono-Si
parameters.notes: Low single-year impact but compounds over 25 years. Year 25 at 0.35%: 91.7% of year 1.

parameters.name: System performance ratio
parameters.description: Ratio of actual AC output to theoretical DC output
parameters.source: Industry standard for C&I rooftop. EPC warranty: 95% PR (vs executive project)
parameters.notes: PR includes: inverter efficiency, wiring losses, soiling, shading, temperature, mismatch. The EPC 95% PR guarantee is vs the executive project design, not vs theoretical maximum.

parameters.name: Default panel tilt angle
parameters.description: Panel tilt angle used as baseline for PVGIS yield lookup. Must match a tilt in the fetched .npz data.
parameters.source: C&I rooftop coplanar convention. Updated from 5° (2026-03-12).
parameters.notes: Available tilts in .npz: 0, 5, 10, 15, 25, 27, 28, 30, 31, 32, 33. Change this value and re-run compute_zone_stats.py to recalibrate. solar_profile.py reads this at runtime — no code edits needed.

parameters.name: PVGIS yield correction factor
parameters.description: Residual gap after zone-specific PVGIS calibration. Field correction for soiling, shading, mismatch.
parameters.source: Calibrated from zone-specific PVGIS data (was 0.82 pre-zone data, now 0.98 post-calibration)
parameters.notes: Universal across zones. Applied after PVGIS P50 specific yield.

parameters.name: Curtailment / sin-excedentes cap
parameters.description: Fraction of production lost to grid injection limits
parameters.source: Averta projects operate con excedentes (Alfe, Mecanizados). Pandrol sin excedentes.
parameters.notes: Sin excedentes: inverter throttles when production > consumption → lost kWh. Con excedentes: surplus injected to grid → compensated at pool price. Most new projects likely con excedentes. Model both modes.

parameters.name: Self-consumption ratio
parameters.description: Fraction of production consumed by community members (not injected as surplus)
parameters.source: Robert call 2026-02-11: 'un 80 es el que conseguimos real.' Target 90%, actual ~80%. Confirmed.
parameters.notes: THIS IS A CRITICAL ASSUMPTION. The 80% is aspirational for a well-matched community. In practice it depends on: number of subscribers, their consumption profiles, occupancy rate, business hours overlap with solar production. Should be calibrated from operational data when available. Beta distribution bounded [0,1] with mode near 0.80.

parameters.name: Consumer occupancy rate
parameters.description: Fraction of community slots filled with paying consumers at any time
parameters.source: Target — 95% initial fill assumes pre-commercialised communities
parameters.notes: Occupancy < 100% means some solar production has no buyer → becomes surplus (valued at pool price, much lower than PPA discount revenue). Raised from 0.90 to 0.95 (2026-03-03). Assumes pre-sold communities with signed adhesion contracts before deployment. Churn risk is the #2 driver after production in the sensitivity analysis.

parameters.name: Annual consumer churn rate
parameters.description: Fraction of consumers who leave per year (business closure, relocation, switch)
parameters.source: Assumption. Spanish SME failure rate ~8-10%/year. Add voluntary churn.
parameters.notes: Churn must be offset by replacement. Net churn (churn - replacement) is what matters. Platform/sponsor risk: can Averta replace churned consumers fast enough? This is the risk taxonomy's 'churn' and 'platform/sponsor' risks combined.

parameters.name: Churn replacement lag
parameters.description: Average months to replace a churned consumer
parameters.source: Assumption — depends on Averta's commercial capacity

parameters.name: Averta discount factor (Fórmula Indexada)
parameters.description: 15% off pre-IE variable rate, no IE charged. See tariff_prices.py and averta_price_derivation.md.
parameters.source: Oferta venta energía 06.02.2026: 15% direct discount on pre-IE rate, IE not charged separately
parameters.notes: This is the core commercial proposition. Fixed by contract for contract duration. Revenue per kWh = consumer's retail rate × 0.7989. If Averta changes this to attract consumers, it directly impacts margin.

parameters.name: Retail tariff — 2.0TD base rate
parameters.description: Average retail tariff for 2.0TD consumers (residential/small commercial) in 2026
parameters.source: CNMC/REE tariff data 2024-2025. Needs validation.
parameters.notes: 2.0TD has 3 periods: punta, llano, valle. The blended rate hides significant period variation. When hourly data available, replace this with period-specific rates from actual bills.

parameters.name: Retail tariff — 3.0TD base rate
parameters.description: Average retail tariff for 3.0TD consumers (commercial/industrial) in 2026
parameters.source: CNMC/REE tariff data. Needs validation from actual bills.
parameters.notes: 3.0TD has 6 periods (P1-P6). Solar hours map primarily to P3-P5 (cheaper periods).

parameters.name: Annual retail tariff escalation (blended)
parameters.description: Blended year-over-year escalation of the 3.0TD tariff, derived from component-level analysis: energy (1%), peaje + cargos (4%). Weights from Eurostat nrg_pc_205_c 2024 Band IC Spain.
parameters.source: Production-weighted 3-component blend (2026-03-03). Using 3.0TD 2026 BOE-sourced peaje/cargo rates × solar production profile (P3-P6 dominant): energy 85.3% × 1% + peaje 4.7% × 4% + cargos 10.0% × 4% = 1.44%. Eurostat band-average (75.9/24.1) overstates regulated weight because solar generates in P5-P6 where peaje ≈ €0.0001/kWh. See P-026 (energy) and P-027 (network) for component justification.
parameters.notes:
Three tariff components with diverging structural trajectories:
1. ENERGY (85.3% of production-weighted tariff, escalation: 1%)
   - Duck curve / wholesale price cannibalization. Spain's PNIEC targets
     81% renewable electricity by 2030, adding ~7 GW solar PV annually.
     Zero marginal cost daytime generation crushes midday wholesale prices
     to zero or negative. For a 3.0TD consumer without storage consuming
     during the day, the energy component is under structural downward
     pressure. Eurostat NRG_SUP CAGR 2017-2024: +2.4% (crisis-inflated);
     pre-crisis 2017-2019: -8.1%.
   - Demand deficit compounds the effect: PNIEC requires +34% demand by
     2030 vs 2019, but actual demand growth is too slow. If demand stays
     flat while supply explodes, zero/negative price frequency increases.

2. PEAJE + CARGOS (14.7% of production-weighted tariff, escalation: 4%)
   - Massive grid investment wave. Spanish grid cannot handle renewables
     influx + electrification (EVs, heat pumps, data centres). Late 2025:
     government raised legal investment caps on grid infrastructure by 62%
     until 2030. Transmission plan: EUR 13.5B by 2030 + EUR 7.7B local
     distribution = EUR 21.2B total. These costs pass through to consumers
     via peajes.
   - If demand doesn't grow to share the EUR 21B+ burden, cost per kWh of
     grid tolls spikes further (fixed costs spread over flat demand base).
   - Eurostat NETC CAGR 2017-2024: +7.7%; 5Y 2019-2024: +9.7%.
     Conservative estimate of 4% is below observed trend.

Blended: 0.853 × 1% + 0.047 × 4% + 0.100 × 4% = 1.44%. Weights from 3.0TD 2026 BOE rates × solar production profile. Eurostat band-average (NRG_SUP/NETC = 75.9/24.1) overstates regulated weight: solar hours concentrate in P5-P6 where peajes are near zero.
Note: pool/surplus compensation (P-024) should escalate at the energy-only rate (1%), not the blended rate, since pool price is wholesale-market-linked and subject to the same cannibalization dynamics.

parameters.name: Energy component escalation
parameters.description: Year-over-year change in the energy & supply component of the 3.0TD tariff. Structural downward pressure from solar PV cannibalization.
parameters.source: Structural analysis of Spanish electricity market (2026-03-03). Duck curve: PNIEC 81% renewable target by 2030, ~7 GW/yr solar additions. Zero marginal cost daytime generation → wholesale cannibalization. Eurostat NRG_SUP (nrg_pc_205_c, ES, Band IC): 2017=0.0803, 2024=0.0946, CAGR +2.4% (crisis-inflated). Pre-crisis 2017-2019: -8.1%. 1% is conservative, accounts for partial recovery post-crisis.
parameters.notes: Drives 85.3% of production-weighted tariff (3.0TD 2026, solar hours). Eurostat band-average understates energy dominance — solar produces in P5-P6 where peajes are negligible. Future component for split-escalation engine implementation. Currently engine uses blended P-023. If PV + storage becomes standard, daytime energy value may recover (peak shifting), but base case assumes continued cannibalization.

parameters.name: Peaje + cargos escalation
parameters.description: Year-over-year change in the regulated network component (peajes + cargos) of the 3.0TD tariff. Structural upward pressure from grid investment.
parameters.source: Structural analysis of Spanish electricity market (2026-03-03). Grid investment wave: government raised infrastructure investment caps by 62% (late 2025). Transmission plan EUR 13.5B + distribution EUR 7.7B = EUR 21.2B by 2030, passed through to consumers via peajes. Demand deficit: PNIEC +34% demand target unlikely → fixed costs spread over flat base → higher per-kWh tolls. Eurostat NETC (nrg_pc_205_c, ES, Band IC): 2017=0.0179, 2024=0.0300, CAGR +7.7%. 5Y 2019-2024: +9.7%. 4% is conservative vs observed trend.
parameters.notes: Drives 14.7% of production-weighted tariff (peaje 4.7% + cargos 10.0%). Peajes and cargos grouped at same rate — both are regulated pass-through of grid investment costs. For autoconsumo value proposition: peaje increases raise the consumer's avoided cost, supporting Averta's pricing ceiling.

parameters.name: Compensación simplificada rate
parameters.description: Comercializadora rate for surplus kWh under compensación simplificada (RD 244/2019 art. 14)
parameters.source: Robert call 2026-02-11: 'entre 40 y 50 €/MWh'. Comercializadora negotiated rate.
parameters.notes: NOT a pool sale. Compensación simplificada: comercializadora compensates consumer for excedentes at a negotiated rate (~€40-50/MWh). Exempt from impuesto eléctrico (5.11%) and peaje de generación (€0.5/MWh). Monthly cap: compensation cannot exceed consumed-from-grid value (bill floor = €0 on energy term). RD 244/2019 art. 14. Averta nets this compensation against its discount (exact mechanism pending Elecsum).

parameters.name: Surplus/pool price escalation
parameters.description: Year-over-year change in the compensación simplificada rate. Wholesale-market-linked — only the energy component. No peaje, no cargos.
parameters.source: Structural analysis (2026-03-03). Pool/surplus compensation is indexed to wholesale market price = energy component only. Unlike autoconsumo (which avoids energy + peaje + cargos), surplus has no regulated network component. Subject to full cannibalization pressure from duck curve / PNIEC solar buildout. Same basis as P-026 (energy_tariff_escalation): 1%.
parameters.notes: Autoconsumo avoided cost = energy + peaje + cargos (3 components, blended 1.44% via P-023). Surplus compensation = energy only (1 component, 1%). This structural asymmetry widens over time: as peajes rise at 4%, the gap between autoconsumo value and surplus value grows — reinforcing the incentive to maximise self-consumption ratio. Engine wired: averta_t uses P-023, pool_t uses P-028 (2026-03-03).

parameters.name: PPA price (blended, from Excel model)
parameters.description: Blended PPA price used in Averta's simplified model
parameters.source: Averta Excel model — Ejemplo 100 kW v2.86
parameters.notes: THIS IS THE SIMPLIFIED MODEL'S APPROXIMATION. In the correct model, revenue = Σ(kWh_period × tariff_period × 0.7989). The €70/MWh is the result of that calculation for a particular consumer mix and tariff structure. We keep it here for validation against the Excel model, then replace with the sumproduct approach when hourly data is available.

parameters.name: O&M cost per kWp
parameters.description: Annual maintenance cost per installed kWp
parameters.source: Averta Excel model (€12/kWp). Industry range €8-15/kWp for C&I rooftop.

parameters.name: Insurance cost per kWp
parameters.description: Annual insurance premium per installed kWp
parameters.source: Averta Excel model (€4/kWp)

parameters.name: Annual rooftop rent
parameters.description: Cash rent paid to rooftop owner per year
parameters.source: Averta Excel model. Contract-specific, varies by rooftop.
parameters.notes: Per rooftop lease contract. Escalates at 1%/year.

parameters.name: Rooftop rent annual escalation
parameters.description: Year-over-year increase in rooftop rent
parameters.source: Rooftop lease contract — Clause 6

parameters.name: Free energy allocation to rooftop owner
parameters.description: Annual kWh allocated free to rooftop owner as part of lease compensation
parameters.source: Contract template — X kWh/year (TBD per contract)
parameters.notes: This is a cost to Averta (foregone revenue). Needs contract-specific data.

parameters.name: O&M cost annual escalation
parameters.description: Year-over-year increase in O&M costs (IPC-linked)
parameters.source: Assumption — linked to Spanish IPC

parameters.name: Platform management fee
parameters.description: Averta central overhead allocated per project as % of revenue
parameters.source: Averta Excel model — not explicitly modeled. TBD.
parameters.notes: Averta's platform cost for billing, monitoring, customer management, regulatory. Not in current model.

parameters.name: Annual consumer payment default rate
parameters.description: Fraction of billed revenue not collected due to non-payment
parameters.source: SEPA Direct Debit (2026-03-03). Mandatory SEPA DD enrolment at contract signature eliminates voluntary non-payment. Residual 1% covers: failed DD (insufficient funds), disputed charges, insolvency. Spanish SME baseline 2-5% reduced by automated collection mechanism.
parameters.notes: Different from churn. Default = consumer exists but doesn't pay. SEPA DD makes non-payment an active opt-out requiring bank revocation, not a passive failure to pay. Contract allows service suspension after 2 missed payments. Multi-offtaker structure means single default is small % of revenue. Reduced from 3% to 1% (2026-03-03).

parameters.name: All-in CAPEX per kWp
parameters.description: Total installed cost including EPC, permits, connection
parameters.source: Averta Excel model (€75,000 / 124.12 kWp = €604.25/kWp)
parameters.notes: AACE Class 3 (budget/feasibility): -20% to +30%. Range: €483 to €786/kWp. Industry benchmark for C&I rooftop Spain 2025-2026: €500-700/kWp all-in.

parameters.name: Inverter replacement cost
parameters.description: Cost to replace inverters at end of warranty period
parameters.source: Industry estimate — inverter ~10% of system cost, replacement in year 10-12

parameters.name: Inverter replacement year
parameters.description: Year in which inverter replacement occurs
parameters.source: Industry practice — 5yr product warranty + typical 10-15yr lifespan

parameters.description: Fraction of CAPEX funded by equity
parameters.source: Equity-only assumption for initial model
parameters.notes: Set to 1.0 (all equity). Override when debt module is built.
